Joystick: the stick tilts by how far you drag from where the thumb landed. Drag: like a mouse; moving the thumb turns, standing still stops.
Double tap: tap twice in a row and keep the thumb down. Leave the zone: slide the thumb out of the stick.
Press the thumb harder against the screen: this button is held for as long as you keep pressing, and let go when you ease off.
Drag only: starts moving a little past what the game ignores.
Progressive trigger: the harder you press, the further the trigger goes. Hold a button: pressing hard also presses the chosen button.
How far you drag to take a stick to its maximum. Applies to both sticks.

Touching again within this time counts as a double tap and the stick keeps moving.

How much bigger your thumb\'s contact must get, against its normal size, to count as squashing. It depends on your phone and thumb, and applies to every control. In "Touch controls and gyroscope" (Settings) with "Show zones" the value shows next to the thumb (for example x1.30 / 1.50).
How far the trigger goes as soon as it is touched.
Progressive trigger: squash for the maximum
How hard the thumb must squash to pull the trigger fully.
Each group works like a stick: the red centre presses nothing, the green ring presses both neighbours at once.

Squashing uses this side\'s thumb calibration: your thumb is measured on this phone, resting, squashing and easing off. If squashing does not respond well, calibrate again. Without it \"Squash strength\" (Fine tuning) is used, which is less reliable.
The triggers use the calibration of the thumb on their side: L2 the left one, R2 the right one (calibrated in each stick\'s section).

For games that do not read the controller\'s gyroscope: moving the phone moves the camera stick, on top of what your thumb does. A button for it appears in the bar while playing.
The speed you turn the phone is how far the stick goes: turn and the camera turns, stop and it stops. Best for aiming. It never needs centring.

How much you tilt it, from where you started, is how far the stick goes: sideways like a steering wheel, forwards and back for up and down. Best for driving and leaning. The centre is where the phone was when it engaged (use Recentre).
Only while the inputs are held
Paused while the inputs are held

"Only while held" suits aiming (L2 is the usual one: you aim and the phone steers). "Paused while held" keeps the gyroscope on all the time and stops it while you hold the inputs: with "right stick" you aim with the phone and, the moment you push the stick with your thumb, the gyroscope goes quiet for the fine adjustment. "Pressing the inputs together" starts off, and the buttons still reach the game. The inputs can be buttons or sticks, several at once (L3 + R3). There is also a gyroscope button for the pad (Controls, in the editor) and the bar\'s one: all of them switch the same thing, and it is remembered.
Tilt for the stick all the way
Movement smaller than this does nothing: the tremor of the hand. Raise it if the camera drifts with the phone still.
Evens out the little jitters, at the cost of a slight delay.
1.00 = proportional. Higher: small movements are finer and big ones fast.
While this one moves the stick, the console gets no gyroscope: a game that reads both would aim twice.
The stick\'s centre goes where the phone is now (Tilt style). In the bar, a long press on the gyroscope button does the same.

The controller the console sees faces forward again, where the device points now (and the gyroscope stick takes it as its centre). It can also be a button of the pad (Controls available) or a key of the physical controller.

Pressing the inputs together switches it on or off

Letting go of the stick takes a moment (a fraction of a second) to count, so a trembling thumb coming back to the middle does not flicker.

Good picture and good stability. Recommended for almost everything.

string-array.name: loss_report_explanations
string-array.item: The console is told nothing is lost: it never adds repair pieces, so a bad network shows as a broken picture (what the original app did).
The console adds a little repair and keeps the quality.
Recommended. The console adds repair pieces without lowering the quality.
More protection, but on a bad network the console starts lowering the quality, and it takes minutes to come back.
More protection, but on a bad network the console lowers the quality, and it takes minutes to come back.
More protection, but on a bad network the console lowers the quality quickly, and it takes minutes to come back.
The whole truth: the most protection, but every bad moment lowers the quality and it hardly comes back during the game.

resources.string:
Your PlayStation, in the palm of your hand. As easy as this:

1. Tap + and register your console. Only once: sign in with your PlayStation account and type the PIN your console shows.

2. Tap its card and play. Quality adjusts by itself to your network and your screen.

3. Mid-game, press Back or tap with three fingers to bring up the bar: touch controller, color, screen modes and exit.

Why Shades? The sunglasses come with a couple of tricks: a lens that fills your screen with no black bars and cinematic color looks, so games shine even on the smallest screen.

Get comfy, grab your controller and let the game begin.
A tip a day on the main screen
A short tip about the app on the main screen, one a day
Before each connection the app picks the bitrate from your network, and the resolution too unless you choose one.
Auto · resolution %1$s, bitrate picked by the app
Auto also lowers it with low battery, heat or a bad network. A fixed one is always kept: then only the bitrate adapts.
When a console can be reached, it shows here what the next connection would ask for and why.
%1$d px screen: more resolution would not show
You sign in on Sony\'s website, in your own browser. This app never sees your password or your Sony session: it only learns your account number, which the console asks for when linking.
1. Open Sony\'s page and sign in.
2. When the page shows \"redirect\", send its address here: Share → Chiaki Shades. Or copy the address and come back.
Signing in with someone else\'s account? Their Sony session stays open in this browser: sign out on Sony\'s site afterwards, or use a private tab.
No browser was found to open Sony\'s page.
The copied text is not Sony\'s \"redirect\" address. Copy the whole address from the browser\'s address bar and try again.
That is not Sony\'s \"redirect\" address (it should contain remoteplay/redirect?code=…).
Sony did not accept the link. Each link works only once and for a few minutes: sign in again and use the new one.
Sony answered something unexpected. Try again later, or enter the Account ID by hand under Advanced.
Could not reach Sony. Check the connection and try again.
A name to tell this account apart (for example your PSN name).
